channel.title: Cadence 步频 — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 50 sources.

item.title: Modest Payment Increases Finalized by CMS for SNFs and IRFs
item.description: CMS finalized modest payment increases for skilled nursing facilities (SNFs) and inpatient rehabilitation facilities (IRFs) for fiscal year 2027, with new rules expected to increase the burden on facilities for delivering, coordinating, and documenting patient care.
item.author: APTA

item.title: Comparative effectiveness of exercise-based prehabilitation before total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
item.description: A systematic review and network meta-analysis compared the effectiveness of various exercise-based prehabilitation modalities before total knee arthroplasty, aiming to clarify optimal approaches.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Efficacy of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation in Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Stimulation Montages and Timing.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 RCTs (419 participants) found active transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) significantly reduced neurological deficits in acute ischemic stroke (WMD=-0.86, 95% CI: -1.38 to -0.34, P=0.001) compared to sham, though no significant improvement in motor function or functional independence was observed.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise Interventions for Older Adults with Alzheimer's Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 142 articles found that exercise interventions can have a small but positive impact on cognitive function in older adults with Alzheimer's disease, but optimal dosage remains unclear.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Foot-Targeted Rehabilitation for Pronation-Related Anterior Knee Pain: A Two-Phase Case-Control Study and Single-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial of Manual Therapy Versus Neuromuscular Training Each With Augmented Low-Dye Taping.
item.description: This two-phase study found foot-targeted manual therapy with augmented low-dye taping (MT + ALDT) and neuromuscular training with ALDT (NMT + ALDT) offered comparable short-term effectiveness to routine physiotherapy for pronation-related anterior knee pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Optimal Exercise Modality and Dose for Blood Pressure Management in Middle-Aged and Older Adults: A Systematic Review with Bayesian Model-Based, and Dose-Response Network Meta-Analysis of RCTs.
item.description: This systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis compared the effects of different exercise modalities and doses on resting systolic and diastolic BP in middle-aged and older adults (≥45 years), identifying optimal approaches for blood pressure management.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of Telerehabilitation Versus Conventional Rehabilitation on Motor Function and Activities of Daily Living After Stroke: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review of four RCTs (N=226) found that telerehabilitation for stroke patients showed noninferiority compared to conventional rehabilitation for motor function (e.g., Fugl-Meyer change adjusted difference 0.06 points, 95% CI -2.14 to 2.26; p = .96) and activities of daily living.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness and feasibility of home-based physical exercise interventions for children and adolescents with chronic diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published up to December 2025 found home-based physical exercise interventions to be effective and feasible in improving aerobic capacity, functional capacity, muscle strength, and quality of life for children and adolescents with chronic diseases.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Effects of battle rope training on sporting performance: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of battle rope training on sporting performance, including upper-limb and lower-limb explosive power, grip strength, upper-limb muscular endurance, and core endurance, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Differences in the Thoracolumbar Fascia Between Low Back Pain Patients and Healthy Individuals: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis confirmed differences in thoracolumbar fascia characteristics between low back pain patients and healthy individuals, highlighting its potential role in LBP.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: Effect of kinesiology taping on limb oedema in patients with severe hyper-dependency using shear-wave elastography: a randomized clinical trial.
item.description: A randomized clinical trial with 50 patients found that kinesiology taping at 25% tension significantly reduced the elastic coefficient of the dermis layer in limb oedema patients compared to 0% tension taping by day 9.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Tapering and Peaking in the Weight Lifting Sports: A Systematic Review of Athletes’ Self-Reported Strategies
item.description: A systematic review compiles self-reported strategies used by athletes for tapering and peaking in weightlifting sports, highlighting common practices.
item.author: Sports Medicine

item.title: A grade-specific clinical prediction rule for independent walking after traumatic spinal cord injury.
item.description: A clinical prediction rule was developed using the National Spinal Cord Injury Statistical Centre dataset (2607 patients) to predict independent walking one year after traumatic SCI, identifying grade-specific predictors.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Joint non-linear dose-response associations of device-measured physical activity and cardiorespiratory fitness with cardiovascular disease: a cohort and Mendelian randomisation study
item.description: A UK Biobank cohort and Mendelian randomization study characterized the non-linear joint dose-response relationship of accelerometer-measured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) and cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) with incident cardiovascular disease (CVD), adjusting for confounders and assessing causal consistency.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Effects of Fingertip Vibrotactile Stimulation on Postural Control in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: A Comparison Across Age Groups
item.description: This study of 348 community-dwelling older adults (65-74, 75-84, 85+ years) found that fingertip vibrotactile stimulation improved postural control (measured by center of pressure velocity and area) across all age groups compared to no stimulation.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Effects of tDCS combined with unstable resistance training on knee muscle strength and neuromuscular control in community-dwelling older adults: a randomized controlled trial
item.description: A randomized controlled trial found that transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) combined with unstable resistance training improved knee muscle strength and neuromuscular control in community-dwelling older adults.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Vancomycin-Soaked Quadriceps Grafts Linked to Early Resorption in ACLR: study
item.description: A study suggests that vancomycin-soaked quadriceps grafts are linked to early resorption following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR).
item.author: Medical Dialogues

item.title: Beyond treatment: how care process factors shape physical therapist management of low back pain.
item.description: This commentary examines how various care process factors, such as timing of care, point of entry, care pathway design, and insurance models, significantly influence patient outcomes in low back pain management, independent of specific treatment interventions.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Intensive, Multi-Technology Rehabilitation Programme for Chronic Stroke Survivors: Outcomes of a Phase I Single-Arm Repeated-Measures Study.
item.description: A Phase I single-arm study found that an 8-week, group-based, multi-technology rehabilitation program led to observed improvements in motor recovery for chronic stroke survivors with persistent motor impairment.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A qualitative inquiry into the environmental barriers and facilitators to non-specific low back pain clinical practice guideline adherence among Canadian physiotherapists.
item.description: A qualitative inquiry explored environmental barriers and facilitators influencing Canadian physiotherapists' adherence to non-specific low back pain clinical practice guidelines, identifying key factors across public and private sectors using the Theoretical Domains Framework and Ecological Systems Theory.
item.author: PubMed
